sources.expected_freshness: near-real-time Sentinel-1 acquisition processing; exact latency is source-dependent
sources.attribution_guidance: Attribute flood event discovery to Copernicus Emergency Management Service Global Flood Monitoring, with EODC as the catalogue and processing host. Observed Flood Extent establishes detected flood pixels only, not severity, impacts, casualties, warnings, or national totals.
limitations: A STAC item or acquisition footprint is not evidence of flooding; a country-clipped ensemble_flood_extent statistic with nonzero class-1 pixels is required.
Country requests use the maintained country polygon in the catalog and omit flood geometry when only positive clipped statistics are available.
Worldwide discovery is a bounded scan of recent GFM items and is not globally complete.
This source does not provide severity, damage, casualties, affected population, warnings, response status, or national flood totals.

sources.organization_name: NASA Earth Observatory Natural Event Tracker
sources.expected_freshness: near-real-time curated event metadata; exact latency is source-dependent
sources.attribution_guidance: Attribute wildfire event discovery to NASA EONET as a curated secondary source. EONET records are not official incident perimeters or national situation reports.
limitations: EONET wildfire curation currently applies a material-size threshold and does not represent every fire or thermal anomaly.
EONET spatial and temporal extents can be approximate and should not be treated as official incident boundaries.
Country requests use the EONET bounding box only for candidate discovery and then validate source geometry against the maintained country polygon.
Worldwide results are a bounded registry query and global completeness is not guaranteed.
This source provides event discovery only; it does not establish acreage beyond a source-reported magnitude, impacts, casualties, warnings, or response status.

sources.organization_name: NASA Fire Information for Resource Management System
sources.display_name: NASA FIRMS event-associated thermal anomaly observations
sources.jurisdiction: global satellite fire and thermal anomaly observations
sources.expected_freshness: VIIRS near-real-time observations are generally available within hours of satellite overpass; coverage has orbital, cloud, sensor, and processing gaps
sources.attribution_guidance: Attribute observations to NASA FIRMS and the VIIRS near-real-time product. Present detections only as possible nearby fire/thermal anomaly pixels associated after an event is selected, never as standalone wildfire events or perimeters.
limitations: A free FIRMS MAP_KEY is required through NASA; the key is never exposed in source URLs, snapshot identities, or reports.
The adapter performs no event discovery and cannot create one event per hotspot. It runs only after a wildfire event with a source-backed point has been selected.

Detections within 50 km are aggregated into one possible-correlation observation report; pixels can represent other thermal sources and do not confirm identity, ignition, perimeter, size, impact, or containment.
VIIRS is not continuous surveillance; clouds, overpass timing, fire intensity, resolution, and processing can cause omissions or spatial overstatement.
GDACS wildfire events are downstream of GWIS, which uses NASA FIRMS detections; agreement between GDACS WF and FIRMS is not independent corroboration.

sources.organization_name: NASA Cooperative Open Online Landslide Repository
sources.expected_freshness: catalog report dates and edits; exact latency is source-dependent
sources.attribution_guidance: Attribute landslide event discovery to NASA COOLR as a secondary report catalogue. COOLR reports can originate from the Global Landslide Catalog, Landslide Reporter, media, external databases, or reviewed citizen submissions.
limitations: COOLR is a global report catalogue rather than complete real-time landslide surveillance.
Reports can originate from media, databases, or reviewed citizen submissions, and geographic and reporting biases remain.
Only documented GLC and LRC import classes are accepted; future classes require an explicit provenance review.
A missing COOLR record is not evidence that no landslide occurred.
This source provides event discovery only; it does not promote casualty, injury, damage, warning, or response fields into event claims.

sources.display_name: Copernicus EMS Rapid Mapping landslide map evidence
sources.expected_freshness: on-demand activation and product delivery; coverage exists only where an authorised user requested Rapid Mapping
sources.attribution_guidance: Credit Copernicus Emergency Management Service Rapid Mapping and link the EMSR activation. Present only delivered feasible delineation or grading products as secondary map evidence associated with an already selected landslide event.
limitations: This provider performs no event discovery. A Rapid Mapping activation is a response request and does not independently prove event identity or occurrence.
Only EMSR Rapid Mapping activations categorized as Mass movement can qualify; Risk and Recovery EMSN preparedness, risk, and recovery assessments are excluded.

An activation qualifies only after same-country, event-time-within-three-days, and centroid-within-100-km checks against a selected source-backed point, followed by a delivered feasible DEL or GRA product check.
Possible correlation is retained because Copernicus and NASA COOLR do not expose a shared stable event identifier through these integrations.
Delineation and grading products apply to requested Areas of Interest and do not establish complete event extent, unmapped impacts, casualties, warnings, response status, or national totals.
The category-filtered public API currently exposes a small set of mass-movement Rapid Mapping activations; absence is not evidence that no landslide occurred.

sources.organization_name: Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System
sources.jurisdiction: global disaster alert and coordination system
sources.expected_freshness: near-real-time event list; exact latency is source-dependent
sources.attribution_guidance: Attribute country-associated or worldwide tropical-cyclone event discovery to GDACS. GDACS alert/model output is not a national warning, local impact assessment, or current-news source.
limitations: Country queries use the structured properties.iso3 primary-country field or properties.affectedcountries[].iso3 affected-country fields, and require a usable point to classify the association against maintained country geometry.
This source provides event discovery only; it is not a national warning, impact report, casualty source, or current-news source.
GDACS alert and model output does not establish local warnings, impacts, casualties, or national totals.

sources.organization_name: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
sources.expected_freshness: IBTrACS v04r01 is updated about three times weekly; the active subset contains storms active within the recent archive window and provisional tracks can lag or change
sources.attribution_guidance: Credit NOAA NCEI IBTrACS v04r01 and retain the IBTrACS SID plus contributing agency and ATCF identifiers. Use the active subset only after a GDACS cyclone is selected and only for conservative track/identity reconciliation, never as live-event authority.
limitations: IBTrACS is a merged retrospective and provisional best-track archive, not a live-event discovery, warning, forecast, impact, or emergency-response authority.

The adapter performs no event discovery and attaches a track only to a GDACS-selected cyclone when a non-generic storm name, track start within 36 hours, and a retained point within 500 km produce exactly one candidate.

The 500 km proximity bound accommodates update latency between the GDACS endpoint and the three-times-weekly active archive; name and start-time agreement are mandatory, and zero or multiple candidates fail closed.
Active-subset observations and identifiers are preliminary and can be revised when operational tracks become best tracks.
IBTrACS merges WMO RSMC, TCWC, JTWC, and other agency records. Those inputs can overlap the upstream agency used by GDACS, so agreement is not independent corroboration.
Wind, pressure, category, landfall, forecast, impact, casualty, warning, and response fields are not promoted by this integration.

sources.organization_name: NOAA National Hurricane Center / Central Pacific Hurricane Center
sources.jurisdiction: Atlantic, Eastern North Pacific, and Central North Pacific operational tropical-cyclone basins
sources.expected_freshness: updated with NHC/CPHC advisories; exact issue and publication latency is source-dependent
sources.attribution_guidance: Credit NOAA NHC/CPHC and retain the ATCF storm identifier, advisory number, product issue time, validity interval, and direct official product URL. Present forecast tracks and cones as advisory geometry, never as observed storm footprints.
limitations: This provider performs no event discovery and runs only after a GDACS tropical cyclone with a source-backed point is selected.

Coverage is limited to active NHC/CPHC products for the Atlantic, Eastern North Pacific, and Central North Pacific basins; absence is reported as unsupported or unavailable forecast context, not as no cyclone.
A layer is attached only when one active storm uniquely matches the selected source name and has an advisory center within 500 km; zero or multiple candidates fail closed.
Only exact source-published forecast positions and cone polygon coordinates are retained. Connecting track segments are a rendering aid and are not forecasts between official points.
The cone depicts probable track-center uncertainty and is not a storm-size, wind, hazard, impact, warning, evacuation, or observed-footprint boundary.
Wind-field shapefiles and unsupported products are excluded; no wind radii or missing geometry are inferred.
NHC/CPHC products can be upstream of GDACS, so agreement is not treated as independent corroboration.

sources.organization_name: Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System
sources.jurisdiction: global disaster alert and coordination system
sources.expected_freshness: event and episode updates are source-dependent; GDACS currently incorporates reviewed GloFAS/FloodList and other authoritative or media-derived reporting
sources.attribution_guidance: Attribute the event to GDACS and retain the per-record GDACS source label such as GLOFAS. This is secondary event discovery, not a source for verified casualties, displacement, severity, national totals, or warnings.
limitations: GDACS flood records are curated from GloFAS/FloodList, ECHO and other authoritative or media sources; they are not independent of the Copernicus/JRC source family.
CEMS GFM and GDACS FL use different products and semantics, but both sit within the Copernicus/EC-JRC ecosystem; agreement is not counted as fully independent corroboration.
The event-list point is a GDACS centroid, not an observed flood extent or official boundary.
GDACS alert levels and model-derived severity are not promoted into impact, casualty, warning, or national-total claims; only the alert label is retained as source-reported severity metadata.
A missing GDACS record is not evidence that no flood occurred.

sources.organization_name: Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System
sources.jurisdiction: global disaster alert and coordination system
sources.expected_freshness: daily when GWIS receives sufficient MODIS/VIIRS imagery, with manual humanitarian-impact additions possible
sources.attribution_guidance: Attribute the event to GDACS and preserve GWIS as the upstream event source. This is secondary event discovery; GDACS/GWIS and direct FIRMS observations are not independent because GWIS uses NASA FIRMS active-fire detections.
limitations: Automatic GDACS wildfire entry normally starts at 5,000 hectares; smaller humanitarian-impact events can be inserted manually, and homepage display applies a stricter filter.
GWIS derives near-real-time burnt-area products using MODIS and VIIRS active-fire detections supplied through NASA FIRMS.
The event-list point is a centroid, not an incident perimeter, ignition point, containment report, or one-hotspot event.
Alert level does not establish casualties, evacuations, damage, warnings, containment, or response status.
A missing GDACS record is not evidence that no wildfire occurred.

sources.organization_name: Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System
sources.jurisdiction: global disaster alert and coordination system
sources.expected_freshness: daily VAA monitoring plus weekly Smithsonian reporting and manual humanitarian-impact updates
sources.attribution_guidance: Attribute the event to GDACS and retain the record's VAAC source label. GDACS VO is secondary discovery/corroboration derived mainly from VAAs and Smithsonian weekly reports, not an independent eruption authority.
limitations: GDACS volcano status depends mainly on Volcanic Ash Advisories and Smithsonian weekly reports; agreement with the directly ingested Smithsonian/USGS WVAR is not independent corroboration.

A VAA establishes an aviation ash advisory, while Smithsonian New Activity/Unrest can include significant activity that is not necessarily a newly confirmed eruption; only records GDACS publishes as VO eruption events are admitted as secondary discovery.
The event-list point is a volcano location, not an ash footprint, exclusion zone, or impact boundary.
GDACS alert level does not establish casualties, evacuations, local warnings, ash concentration, or response status.
A missing GDACS record is not evidence that no eruption occurred.

sources.expected_freshness: near-real-time EMSC-RTS catalogue; event parameters can be revised as observations and analyses change
sources.attribution_guidance: Credit EMSC/CSEM and link the SeismicPortal event. Treat EMSC as scientific event discovery and corroboration, not as an emergency warning or independent confirmation when its preferred origin comes from the same contributing network as another catalogue record.
limitations: The EMSC real-time catalogue can be incomplete, delayed, erroneous, or revised and is not emergency authority.
Preferred event parameters aggregate contributed seismological observations; matching EMSC and USGS records are not automatically independent corroboration.
Country membership is validated against maintained country geometry, with tightly bounded offshore association only when the source region explicitly names the country.

This integration admits hypocentre, depth, magnitude, identity, and catalogue update time only; felt reports, tsunami indications, impacts, casualties, and warnings are not promoted into event claims.

sources.expected_freshness: near-real-time catalog; exact latency is unknown
sources.attribution_guidance: Attribute scientific earthquake records to USGS.
limitations: Country membership uses packaged bounds and simplified polygons.

sources.organization_name: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
sources.expected_freshness: report publication based; exact latency is unknown
sources.attribution_guidance: Present as supplementary preliminary reporting, not an official national total.
limitations: Not an event-verification source.
Provider-local IDs are not comparable to event-provider IDs.

sources.organization_name: Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program / U.S. Geological Survey Volcano Hazards Program
sources.display_name: Smithsonian / USGS Weekly Volcanic Activity Report
sources.expected_freshness: weekly report publication; exact source update timing is source-dependent
sources.attribution_guidance: Attribute admitted eruptive-activity event discovery to the Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program / USGS Volcano Hazards Program. GVP volcano metadata supplies source-backed identity and coordinates.
limitations: WVAR is preliminary and is not a comprehensive list of all eruptions.
Routine long-running activity can be omitted, and rapidly developing events can be covered only fragmentarily.
Absence from WVAR is not evidence that no eruption is occurring.
Only explicit New Eruptive Activity and Continuing Eruptive Activity report types are admitted; unrest and other observations are deliberately excluded from volcanic-eruption events.
Event discovery does not establish casualties, evacuations, infrastructure impacts, local warnings, exclusion zones, or response status.
WVAR summaries may cite national observatories, but DisasterMonitor does not independently ingest those embedded authorities through this provider.
sources.provider_registration_name: Smithsonian / USGS Weekly Volcanic Activity Report

sources.jurisdiction: United States land areas served by the National Weather Service
sources.expected_freshness: active pull feed; NWS recommends requesting no more often than every 30 seconds, while alert issue and retrieval times remain distinct
sources.attribution_guidance: Attribute warning artifacts to NOAA/National Weather Service and retain the issuing NWS office shown on each alert.
limitations: Coverage is limited to active NWS alerts for United States land areas and is not global.
Many zone-based alerts and watches have no polygon geometry; missing geometry is not reconstructed from place names or zone labels.
The pull API can be delayed or unavailable and is not a replacement for official local warning channels.
Alerts are separate warning artifacts and never confirm or discover a physical disaster event, impact, casualty, or evacuation.
